The test image shows a soybean leaf upper surface with numerous small spots — yellow-green halos surrounding darker brown centers, scattered across the leaf. Key observations:
- Small discrete spots with yellow halos
- Dark brown to reddish-brown centers
- Distributed across the whole leaf surface
- Not angular/vein-limited
- No white powdery coating

Top candidates: Downy mildew (yellow spots on upper surface), Bacterial_Pustule (light spots with raised centers), Frogeye_leaf_spot (gray centers with reddish-brown borders). Let me check the reference.

The downy mildew reference shows pale yellowish-green diffuse spots on the upper surface — distinct from test image which has more discrete spots with prominent yellow halos and darker brown centers.

Comparing all evidence:
- Test image: small discrete spots with **prominent yellow halos** and dark brown centers, scattered non-angularly across upper leaf surface
- Downy mildew description: "small light green spots that enlarge and turn pale to bright yellow" — yellow halos match, and darker centers = older lesions browning
- Downy mildew reference shows the same scattered pale yellow spots pattern on upper leaf surfaces
- Bacterial pustule would have LESS chlorosis/yellowing around lesions (ruled out by prominent halos)
- Frogeye would show gray centers with reddish-brown borders (not quite matching)

The scattered yellow spots with aging darker centers on the upper leaf surface strongly align with **Downy mildew**.
